purpose: Editorial companion engravings for the Atlas; allegories, not literal scenes attributed to Goethe
preparation: WebP resizing/compression only; fading and blending remain non-destructive CSS

images.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: a quiet editorial illustration for a software website inspired by Goethe's Faust and land reclaimed FROM the sea. This is not a literal scene claim about the play, it is an editorial allegory. Render as an exquisite 19th-century scientific atlas plate: finely etched Prussian-blue copperplate linework, delicate crosshatching, soft desaturated blue-grey watercolor washes on very pale cool paper (#e9eef0), tiny restrained dark red detail at most. Match a sophisticated literary atlas aesthetic, anatomically convincing people in early-modern European work clothing. Landscape 1536x1024 composition. No text, letters, numbers, borders, captions, logos, UI or watermark. No fantasy glow, robots, computer gear, monsters, gothic castle or saturated colors. Detailed but airy, moderate low contrast, large breathing space; preserve the readable silhouette of the central subject. The drawing must gradually dissolve into clean pale paper at ALL edges, especially bottom and sides: floating open vignette, never a rectangular photograph or framed plate. We will further soften with CSS, so keep fine lines visible.
Primary request: The historian of the reclamation works. An observant middle-aged chronicler with short greying beard, round spectacles and plain dark blue-grey coat, seated at a modest timber desk under a simple open shelter, recording the day in a large open field notebook with a quill. His head and hand are bent attentively over the writing. A second rolled survey plan and a few bound ledgers sit beside him; their pages show only faint non-linguistic pen marks, no readable writing. Seen in three-quarter side view, medium-wide framing, figure and desk form the main focus in the center-right half of the canvas. In the pale distant background at left, a small unfinished stone dike and faint sea suggest that he is documenting an active worksite. The notebook, writing hand and face should be distinct even when displayed faintly. Avoid depicting the existing elderly Fausto contemplating a map; this is a working chronicler, recording rather than dreaming. Nothing theatrical. Leftmost 20% and topmost 15% mostly empty paper.

Primary request: Three distinct craftspeople working on one small section of a stone sea dike, the allegory for separate software test writer, implementer and reviewer. A compact composition of exactly THREE human figures: at left a surveyor uses a measuring rod and a small drawn plan to specify the dimensions; in the middle a mason carefully seats one squared stone; at right a different inspector checks the built stonework with a plumb line and square. Their separate actions are immediately legible, each has only the tools for their task. Quiet concentration, mutual orientation, not posing for camera. Stone course in foreground, very faint water and timber scaffolding behind. All action in the center and lower-middle region, wide airy margin. The low dike is under construction against the sea; not an urban street or cathedral building. No captions or arrows, no triptych panels. A single unified delicate engraving.

Primary request: An elevated oblique survey view of newly reclaimed land enclosed by a strong curved sea dike. Clearly show open sea OUTSIDE the barrier at upper right and dry land that was previously underwater INSIDE it. Three distinct reclaimed polders have low earthen boundaries and are connected by narrow drainage channels, small timber bridges and carefully placed sluice gates. A few tiny early-modern buildings, sparse paths and geometric cultivation lines make the land usable, but no large city. It is a geographical landscape, not a software flowchart. The main composition sweeps diagonally across the central and right areas, with very pale empty paper at left and edges. Delicate ordered cadastral marks with no labels. Show clear boundaries AND crossings; this is the image for modular domains communicating via events. Quiet open horizon, human-scale ambition, order earned from the sea. Avoid an island in a lake; the large dike separates the ocean from reclaimed terrain.
